findings.telemetry: All 37 live codegraph rows in .claude/logs/intel-bus.jsonl show duration_ms 34875-49979 (sampled: 34875, 39636, 49979, 40551, 44525, 42250). The boundary contract calls codegraph 'broad, fast, FTS-first'.
findings.observe_how: With 3+ dirty/untracked files (any extension - .md/.json count too), time `node scripts/code-intel.mjs find-symbol Foo` and count spawned codegraph node processes. Each dirty file = one ~3-8s process spawn, re-paid on every facade call because _freshnessDone/_gitHeadCache are per-process and each CLI call is a new process; only the .indexed-head stamp persists, and it only tracks HEAD, not worktree dirt. Note syncWholeProject already does the same work in ONE spawn ('sync -q root'), so the per-file loop is strictly worse whenever dirty count > 1; worst case is 200 spawns (~13+ min). The rule's 'amortized by the freshness cache' claim is disproven by the live durations.

coverage_manifest: scripts/code-intel.mjs end-to-end (1130 lines): READ in full. Two S1, four S2, three S3 findings (D4b-01..10); everything else clean.

runCodegraph npm-shim spawn: CLEAN - invokes process.execPath + real npm-shim.js entrypoint, array args, cwd=repoRoot, windowsHide:true, no shell:true; matches the C.1 platform contract exactly (lines 374-401).

kill-switch order: CLEAN - codegraphAbsent() checks CCV3_KILLSWITCH then CCV3_CODEGRAPH_OFF then resolved-binary-missing, lazily on every call (lines 365-370); CCV3_BUS_OFF independently gates bus read + telemetry, consistent with context-bus.ts/intel-bus.ts which use only CCV3_BUS_OFF. Note: CCV3_KILLSWITCH exists ONLY in this facade (no other hooks-src consumer) - naming implies global scope it does not have; not raised as a finding.

freshness probe + .indexed-head stamp: codex fix #1 is present and stamp-test-covered, BUT the incremental branch spawns one codegraph process per dirty file on every call (D4b-01, S1), the force path can permanently loop under the 60s timeout (D4b-07, S2 INFERRED), and the provenance it returns 'for telemetry' is never emitted (D4b-08, S3). Stamp file correctly ignored via .codegraph/.gitignore ('.indexed-head' entry verified) and .gitignore line 237 ('.codegraph/').

toScipId: collision-safe for fully-populated nodes (hash = uri|lang|qualifiedName|kind|startLine, unit-tested); persistable guard does NOT enforce its documented filePath-or-qualifiedName invariant - bare name passes (D4b-04, S2).

corpus_signature: CLEAN - real `git ls-files` enumeration (file_count 2804 matches live rows), .gitignore sha fingerprint, fail-open to null, cached per process. Minor comment drift only: 'codegraph status fileCount kept as a cross-check' is claimed but no cross-check exists anywhere (not raised - S3 cap).

cgArgs '--' guard (codex fix #2): CORRECT for codegraph - flags first, '--' separator, user positional last; unit + e2e tested (find-symbol --version). Asymmetry: tldr/recall fallback args remain unguarded (D4b-09, S3).

validateCgShape (codex fix #3): CORRECT - distinguishes valid-empty (stay on codegraph) from wrong-shape (fall back to TLDR) for 'array' and object-with-key kinds; 9-case unit test + live valid-empty probe. Gap: the code-context impact augment bypasses it (any status-0 object accepted, arrays included) - folded into D4b-10.

who-calls path narrowing (codex fix #4): CORRECT - client-side fileUri substring filter matches the TLDR fallback's impact-path semantics; live narrow/retain tests present. Serena-escalation hint fires on empty or alias-prone names per the C.1 edge-orphaning caveat.
field-sparse persistable filter (codex fix #5): PRESENT but NOT correct per its own spec - see D4b-04. Shipped test only exercises name:'' so the name-only collision is untested.

proposed_bus_updates TTL: emitted correctly (persistable-only hashes, git_sha + corpus_signature validity stamp, only on live codegraph runs - OFF-path absence is tested), but NO consumer exists; the 'downstream SubagentStop writer' in code comment and rule is fictional in present tense (D4b-03, S2).

scripts/code-intel.test.sh coverage (317 lines): READ in full. Solid on routing/clarify/kill-switch/sanitization/telemetry/cgArgs/validateCgShape/stamp. Gaps: code-context entirely untested (D4b-10); nested-cwd test at line 83 creates junk scripts/.claude on every run (D4b-06/SEED-06); stamp test at lines 295-313 writes the REAL repo's .codegraph/.indexed-head and triggers a live sync (restores the stamp afterward - accepted, noted); no positive assertion that codegraph rows carry subject_id/corpus_signature.

.claude/rules/code-intel-boundaries.md contract: Phase C status, kill-switch order, edge-orphaning caveat, and single-writer rule all match the code. Three claims do not survive contact: 'amortized by the freshness cache' (D4b-01 - telemetry shows 35-50s), the present-tense SubagentStop writer (D4b-03), and 'L3 specialists READ the bus to bias queries' which is unimplemented on the who-calls/find-symbol hot paths (D4b-05).

intel-bus rows vs code claims: 37 codegraph rows = 35 'codegraph' + 2 'codegraph+tldr+archival_memory', exactly the specialist values the code emits; field set matches the appendIntelRow allowlist (no raw symbol names/paths - redaction-by-construction claim HOLDS; subject_id is a 32-hex hash, corpus_signature fingerprint-only). Mismatches: bus_id 'unknown' on 35/37, agent never set, correlation_id ties nothing (D4b-05); code-context rows lack result_count (D4b-10).

codegraph 'impact' subcommand existence: VERIFIED real - dist/bin/codegraph.d.ts:21 documents 'codegraph impact <symbol>' (checked in node_modules for verification only, not cited as finding evidence); the boundary rule's code-context = query + impact fusion is implementable as written.

code-intel-enforcer.ts (adjacent hook nudging toward the facade): CLEAN - default OFF, never denies, exact structural match only; its 'broad, FTS-first' speed framing inherits the D4b-01 latency contradiction and its suggested relative-path command inherits D4b-06's nested-cwd hazard if ever enabled; no separate finding.
